A sumptuous finish by Carlos Forbs, a second-half substitute, was ultimately enough to clinch victory on a topsy-turvy night with Portugal surviving Pedro Neto’s sending-off for two yellow cards. Turn a new page and all that. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued the new rule in July to eliminate what the department described as the "'duration of status' loophole," which it said had allowed foreign students, exchange visitors, and media representatives to remain in the country indefinitely. Dennis Saylor IV of Massachusetts vacated the rule, finding it arbitrary and capricious because the department had failed to weigh the costs and benefits of implementing it. Sometimes they are electrifying and sometimes they are deathly dull. Sometimes they are completely baffling. My absolute favourite kind of show is the one that makes me want to run home and change my outfit. A show that makes me think: there it is! That’s exactly what I want to wear. When the look speaks to me, as if it had been on the tip of my tongue. God, I love that. Which is what happened at Prada this season . The idea was: skirts. That’s it, that’s the whole idea. The show was 63 different skirts – some with a sweater, some with a bra top, some with a jacket, but the point was the skirts. They were knee-length, give or take an inch up or down, and A-line, although sometimes a narrow almost-pencil and other times with a broader flare. There were skirts that wrapped like kilts, held together with strips of industrial-weight Velcro embroidered with tiny gems. records.title: Touch of evil: the terrifying truth about sleep paralysis
records.summary: One in five people have experienced this frightening state – and the Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal has dedicated his career to studying it. Could it be a portal to a deeper understanding of the mind? The Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal is considering the unfathomable depths of the human brain. “It can contemplate itself, and vast galaxies, spirits, souls, poetry, Einstein. Yet you hold it in your hand and it seems so trivial.” Jalal’s passion – the subject that drove him to become a scientist – is sleep paralysis, a brain glitch that can fill its host with terror so palpable that it can cause lasting trauma. “What you get very close to in sleep paralysis,” he says, “is that subjective world of the mind. It’s very hard to put into words.” He should know – he’s spent 271 pages trying to do so. His new book, The Phantom Mind, argues that by exploring the borderlands of sleep, where sleep paralysis occurs, we can delve deeper into how all aspects of our minds work. He may wear a lab coat and examine brain regions and neurochemicals, but studying the mechanics, he says, doesn’t damp down the mysteries of consciousness. “For me, actually, I’ve become more spiritual and interested in the world of mystery and, I want to say supernatural, but dimensions that are intangible, by studying something like sleep paralysis.” Continue reading...

records.title: "Birds of War": New Film Tells a Story of Love and Journalism from Syria to Lebanon
records.summary: We speak with Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak, filmmakers and subjects of the new documentary Birds of War , which tells their epic love story through years of upheaval in the Middle East. Boulos, a London-based Lebanese journalist working for the BBC , and Habak, a Syrian activist and cameraman, first connected while covering the Syrian civil war and stayed in touch through years of war, revolution and exile, forming a relationship that is chronicled in the documentary by drawing on 13 years of their personal videos, voice notes and other correspondence. The film also examines the unequal relationship between international news organizations and local journalists whose work they rely on, the fraught political history between Syria and Lebanon, and how Boulos and Habak’s personal connection overcame those divisions. “Without our journalistic relationship, [we] would have never been together. I would have never opened my heart to somebody like him,” says Boulos. “We can be any race, any gender, any religion, any background, but at the same time we’re all humans.” Birds of War premiered at the 2026 Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Documentary Special Jury Award for Journalistic Impact.

records.title: Meet David Morales: Providence Voters Elect Democratic Socialist Mayor, Approve Israel Divestment
records.summary: Voters in Providence, Rhode Island, approved a ballot measure last week that could result in the city divesting from Israel. The successful grassroots campaign makes Providence the first U.S. city to pass a binding divestment measure through a popular vote. The measure instructs the city to divest from countries and companies implicated in “ethnic cleansing, apartheid, illegal military occupation, or genocide.” The language does not mention Israel by name. We speak with one of the key backers of the divestment measure, Mayor-elect David Morales, a 28-year-old democratic socialist who made history on election night as the youngest mayor ever elected in Providence. “What we saw was our neighbors coming out in the thousands to demonstrate that we are ready for change,” Morales says, promising to enact his affordability-focused platform. “It’s the responsibility of local government to take action. And for that reason, we are seeing a rise in democratic socialism and the representation of democratic socialists all across the country.”

records.title: "American Scoundrel": From Roy Cohn to Stephen Miller, "McCarthyism Lives On," Says Author Kai Bird
records.summary: We speak with historian Kai Bird about American Scoundrel , a new biography of the notorious political fixer Roy Cohn, who rose to fame as chief counsel to Joe McCarthy during the senator’s anti-communist campaign, served as a lawyer for the New York mob, and was an influential voice in Republican circles until his death from AIDS -related complications in 1986. His most impactful relationship, however, would prove to be with a young Donald Trump, whom he mentored in business and politics during the 1970s and ’80s. Facing political setbacks during his first term as president, Trump reportedly asked, “Where’s my Roy Cohn?” Bird, who co-authored American Scoundrel with his wife Susan Goldmark, says Trump may have found his Cohn in Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration’s mass deportation policies whom Trump just elevated to chief of staff. “It’s not really a surprise that, cornered and wounded by the recent election results, he reaches out and pulls up Stephen Miller, who’s very similar in his willingness to go on the offensive and never back down, and to say outrageous things to try to change the narrative,” says Bird.

Meanwhile, progressive Democrat Dr. Abdul El-Sayed defeated former Republican Congressmember Mike Rogers for an open Senate seat in Michigan with over 52% of the vote. El-Sayed campaigned on a platform of Medicare for All, tackling economic inequality and getting big money out of politics — as well as ending military aid to Israel. He is the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate. El-Sayed faced vitriolic, Islamaphobic attacks by top Republicans throughout the campaign. “Last night wasn’t just about Dr. Abdulrahman being a Muslim, winning and going to the United States Senate,” says Palestinian American organizer and author Linda Sarsour, who has been campaigning for El-Sayed. “It demonstrated that progressives can win in states like Michigan” and that “we can win on standing up for the human rights of the Palestinian people.”

methodology.reliability: A official primary source/catalogue; B established newsroom or independent research; C specialist, advocacy or aggregator; D alternative commentary; E unverified social/community; U unclassified. Grade describes source class, not the truth of a specific claim.
methodology.confidence: Claim confidence is left unassessed unless an upstream collector supplies a numeric value. Source grade is not claim confidence.
methodology.corroboration: The six views reuse the existing archive. Similar stories, repeated posts, syndicated copy or multiple outlets quoting one origin are not independent corroboration. A human must inspect provenance.
methodology.geolocation: Location is shown only when supplied by the source or upstream archive. No location is inferred from a headline.
methodology.limits: This is open-source situational awareness, not intelligence agency coverage, an emergency warning service, a live market terminal or a verified threat assessment.
